definition: Open-source robotics is a branch of robotics where robots are developed with open-source hardware and free and open-source software, publicly sharing blueprints, schematics, and source code.
details: It is thus closely related to the open design movement, the maker movement and open science.

explainer.lead: Open-source robotics is a branch of robotics in which robots are developed with open-source hardware and free and open-source software, with blueprints, schematics, and source code shared publicly. It matters because it lets others build on and reproduce robot designs.

tiers.eli5: It's building robots and posting the plans and code online so anyone can copy or improve them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers share schematics and source code so others can rebuild or extend a robot platform. Pitfall: publicly shared designs can be reused in ways the original developers don't control.
tiers.paperLevel: A branch of robotics where robots are developed with open-source hardware and free and open-source software, publicly sharing blueprints, schematics, and source code; closely related to the open design movement, the maker movement, and open science.

explainer.example: A team publishes a robot's blueprints, schematics, and source code; another group builds the same robot from them.
